subject: Post-call: pricing metrics and token vs request clarification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks — quick pricing clarifications from today

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap + a couple of clarifying questions so we can put together a tight estimate for your finance team.

Recap (high level):
- Primary use case: document summarization + triage for care teams (batch + on-demand).
- Expected users: 1,500 active monthly.
- Two patterns: chunked batch processing (nightly jobs) and interactive summarization (on-demand via web UI).

Pricing/volume items we need to confirm:
1) Volume: you mentioned ~10M characters/day in batch and ~3 requests/user/month (interactive). Can you confirm whether the 10M characters is the pre-token characters (i.e., raw text) or already estimated tokens?
2) Metric preference: your procurement team asked about billing per request vs per token. For clarity: Redwood bills primarily on tokens (input + output). Requests is a convenience metric but unit economics are driven by tokens.
3) Caching: are you planning to cache the full prompt+context results for the interactive flows? If prompts are identical and we can serve from prefix/KV caching, billed tokens drop significantly — we charge tokens generated/served, not requests cached.

For the estimate I plan to model a couple of scenarios and show $/1M tokens numbers (we know procurement likes seeing target $/1M tokens). If you can reply with:
- avg characters per request (interactive) and avg tokens per request if you have it,
- confirmation whether the 10M characters/day is raw text or token estimate,
- any hard budget target (e.g., target $/1M tokens, or monthly budget range),
that will help us produce the numbers quickly.

I'll loop Ben in for a worked example once we have the numbers.

Thanks — talk soon,

Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — good recap. Couple quick answers and a clarification request from our side:

- The 10M characters/day is raw characters (pre-tokenization). We don't have tokens calculated yet.
- For the interactive flow: average prompt is ~1,200 characters and average response ~600 characters. That's currently across an expected 3 requests/user/month for the 1,500 users.
- Procurement asked if we can pay per "request" (they like the simplicity) — but they also asked for a target unit economics figure of $X per 1M tokens. They didn't give a number; they asked us to ask vendors for a competitive $/1M tokens.

One more question: if Redwood's caching can de-duplicate prompts (i.e., if many clinicians use the same template prompt), how does that show up in billing? Do we bill the request but not tokens if cached, or does it reduce billed tokens?

Great notes — jumping in with a worked example so procurement has something concrete to react to.

Assumptions (we can adjust):
- 10M characters/day (batch) -> rough token conversion: typical English token ~= 4 chars, so 10M chars/day ≈ 2.5M tokens/day -> ~75M tokens/month. (This is a rule-of-thumb; we'll refine with exact tokenizer if you want.)
- Interactive: 1,200 chars in + 600 chars out -> 1,800 chars/request -> ~450 tokens/request. At 1,500 users * 3 requests/month = 4,500 requests/month -> ~2.025M tokens/month interactive.
- Combined: ~77M tokens/month.

Unit economics examples:
- If target is $20 / 1M tokens -> monthly = 77 * $20 = $1,540. (Note: numbers simplified; Redwood billing includes both input+output tokens counted).
- If target is $10 / 1M tokens -> monthly = 77 * $10 = $770.

Regarding caching vs billed tokens: short answer — we bill tokens that are actually served by the model. If a request is fully served from a cache (exact prompt + same model result), there is no model execution and therefore minimal billed tokens (usually just a small lookup/op cost we can model). For prefix/KV caching we still charge only for tokens not reconstructed from cache; in practice, if the cached result avoids model generation entirely, billed tokens can go to near-zero for that request. This is why prompt deduplication and response-level caching can have an outsized impact on $/1M tokens.

Next steps I can do:
- Build a 3-scenario cost model (pessimistic/expected/optimistic) and return it as an XLSX (will include $/1M tokens, monthly totals, and notes on where caching helps).
- Show a conservative tokenizer-based conversion and an exact run-through if you can share a small sample file (we can token-count locally, not shared externally).

I'm attaching a quick token_cost_calc.csv for the simple calc.
